children: Canadian trade figures for July were soft but largely were a look in the rearview mirror as the trade landscape has shifted again, says Bank of Montreal's Shelly Kaushik. The merchandise-trade surplus narrowed to roughly C$800 million from C$4.2 billion in June, with exports down on lower energy and metals, though both remain historically elevated. Kaushik says the recent round of U.S. tariffs threatened in mid-July and effective mid-August, and Canadian countermeasures set for early September, will add additional noise to trade data in the coming months. The economist anticipates some tariff front-running to support imports and exports through the first half of August before weighing heavily from September. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)
